title: Nx to Graph IR v1 extractor (real, non-spike)
objective: Implement the real Nx to Graph IR v1 extractor that produces docs/generated/grafting.graph.json (project/target nodes, contains/depends_on edges) conforming to docs/graph-ir/graph-ir-v1.schema.json, per master source S16.7/S23 and S27's open 'grafting.graph.json' checklist line, without touching the frozen spike files or the Architecture Studio spike viewer (deferred to I-006).
validations: node tools/scripts/graph-ir-extract.mjs then --check: converges (47 nodes, 43 edges), including after a deliberate hand-edit-then-regenerate drift-detection check

node --test tools/scripts/graph-ir-extract.test.mjs: 6/6 passing, including real collision-case assertions (architecture-studio->graph-x6 collapses implicit+static to one declared edge; isekai-web-client->@grafting/isekai-wasm is derived+confidence<1; architecture-studio's Nx-inferred dev target is derived_evidence) and a direct RFC 6901 unit test of jsonPointerEscape
node --test tools/scripts/validate-graph-ir.test.mjs: 11/11 passing (existing I-002 suite, unaffected)

extractor's own self-check ran both validation layers on every invocation: Ajv schema + JS semantic validation (validate-graph-ir.mjs) and the real Rust graph-ir-cli binary (cargo run -p grafting-graph-core --features graph-ir-cli --bin validate-graph-ir), per DEC-051

docs/generated/grafting.graph.spike.json refreshed via its own existing generator (generate-graph-ir.mjs) after the new task record changed .ai/state/tasks/ content, then re-verified --check current -- routine housekeeping, not a redesign of the spike's shape
uv run --package automation python -m automation.coordination --root .: passed (19 tasks)

git status --short confirmed only this task's declared affected_paths changed on top of Codex's separate concurrent work; grafting.graph.spike.json's regeneration is content-only (refreshed via its own generator), packages/graph-x6 and apps/architecture-studio/src/main.ts untouched
risks: Nx's real project-graph.json records the same (source,target) dependency pair under two different types (implicit+static) in real current cases (architecture-studio->graph-x6, graph-x6->x6-canvas); the v1 schema's canonical edge ID has no room for a type suffix, so edges are collapsed one per pair (declared+confidence 1 if an implicit/authored declaration exists, else derived+confidence 0.95 otherwise) rather than emitted per spike convention. Confirmed empirically and covered by a real test.

sourceRevision's workspace:sha256 dirty-fingerprint is new logic with no prior implementation in this repo. A Plan-review pass caught that scoping it to a whole-repo git status scan is self-referential (the generator's own output becomes part of the working tree once written, so --check could never converge); fixed by scoping strictly to the extractor's own real inputs (project-graph.json + manifests read), confirmed by real --check convergence.

Per DEC-051, structural invariants (unique IDs, edge endpoint existence) are authoritative in Rust grafting-graph-core, not reimplemented in TypeScript; the extractor's self-check runs the real graph-ir-cli Rust binary against the generated output on every invocation, not just the JS validator (a Plan-review pass caught that the first draft's own ad hoc JS duplicate-ID guard would have duplicated that authority).

Scope deliberately excludes task/agent/handoff/skill/prompt nodes (spike-era coverage) -- Nx-sourced data only, matching the backlog item's own title and criterion; independently corroborated by Codex's G-005 handoff, which names the same boundary. A later I-006-or-later/J-012 extractor is expected to cover that side.

A new Claude Code runtime guard (COORDINATION-CLAUDE-RUNTIME-GUARD, owned by codex, still in_progress at completion) now enforces claim-before-edit via .claude/settings.json; this task record's creation satisfied it. One real friction it did not anticipate: it also blocks Claude Code's own Plan Mode file (outside the repo tree) -- surfaced to the owner directly, who approved the reviewed plan verbally in-conversation instead of through the file-based flow this one time.

Architecture Studio spike viewer migration (moving off grafting.graph.spike.json onto the real v1 file, removing graph-x6) is I-006, a separate backlog item, not started here -- I-004 only supplies the data it will need.
